exercise1.prompt: Round at the end, and show the precision you actually have.

hiddenCases.name: a single value is its own mean and both ends
the mean is computed, not copied from an end
the spread is reported next to the middle
hiddenCases.describe: the smallest and largest values alongside the mean

exercise1.hint: Compute all three, round each to one place with float() so they print as plain numbers, and build the sentence with an f-string.

questions.prompt: Why round at the end rather than as you go?
choices: Rounding early loses precision that the later steps then compound
questions.explain: Every intermediate rounding is an error carried forward. Rounding is a presentation step, not a calculation step.

questions.prompt: What does reporting a mean to six decimal places suggest?
choices: A precision the measurements do not support
questions.explain: Digits are a claim about accuracy. Showing more than you have is a quiet form of overstating the result.

questions.prompt: Why report the minimum and maximum next to a mean?
choices: Because the mean alone hides the spread
questions.explain: Two numbers turn a figure that can mislead into one a reader can weigh.
